acceptance_criteria.criterion: csCloseModal() calls .focus() on the element that was active when the modal was opened
Focus restoration is safe when csTriggerElement is document.body or a detached element (no error thrown)
csTriggerElement is nulled after focus restoration to avoid stale references

summary: Added `var csTriggerElement = null;` to the module-level state block in config-stores.js, alongside the existing csClickHandler and other state variables.
Captured `csTriggerElement = document.activeElement;` as the first statement in `csRenderStoreModal()` before any DOM manipulation, covering both Add and Edit flows.

Modified `csCloseModal()` to restore focus to csTriggerElement (guarded with `typeof .focus === 'function'`) after overlay removal and before state nulling; nulls csTriggerElement afterward to prevent stale references.
Verified 3944 existing tests pass with zero regressions.

comments.note: The comment block for the state variables (config-stores.js L11–L22) does not document csTriggerElement. A follow-up or the QA agent could add a line describing the variable's purpose alongside the other entries. The implementation intentionally omits this to keep scope minimal.

summary: Verified AC1: csRenderStoreModal() captures document.activeElement as its first statement (config-stores.js:205, before any DOM manipulation). csCloseModal() calls csTriggerElement.focus() at lines 299–301.

Verified AC2: Guard `if (csTriggerElement && typeof csTriggerElement.focus === 'function')` is safe for document.body (focus() exists, no throw) and detached elements (focus() still on HTMLElement.prototype, calling it silently no-ops in all browsers — no throw).
Verified AC3: csTriggerElement = null on line 302 is unconditional (outside the if-block), executes regardless of whether focus was restored.

Edge-case checks: csCloseModal() without prior modal open (csTriggerElement null → guard short-circuits, no crash); document.activeElement null at open time (null stored, guard short-circuits); 3947 tests pass, zero regressions (3944 at implementation time + 3 new unrelated GUI tests).

comments.note: config-stores.js has no automated tests (it is browser-only frontend JS). All three ACs were verified by code inspection and manual reasoning. A future task could add JSDOM-based unit tests for csRenderStoreModal/csCloseModal focus behaviour.

If csRenderStoreModal() is called while a modal is already open (re-render path), the existing overlay is removed without calling csCloseModal(), so csTriggerElement is overwritten with document.activeElement at re-render time (likely a modal input). This is a pre-existing architectural choice, not a regression from this WP, and no AC is affected.

summary: All three acceptance criteria verified by code inspection. Implementation is minimal, correct, and follows established ES5 module-level state patterns precisely.
Fix-Forward applied: added csTriggerElement description to the module-level state comment block (L11-22), which previously documented 7 of 9 variables and was missing an entry for this new variable.

Focus restoration ordering in csCloseModal() is architecturally correct: overlay removed → focus restored (guarded) → csTriggerElement nulled unconditionally → other state nulled. The unconditional null placement (outside the if-guard) is the right choice — nulling runs regardless of whether focus() was called.
No blocking issues found. No new dependencies, no new patterns, no regressions (3947/3947 tests pass).

comments.note: Added csTriggerElement entry to the state comment block (L11-22). The block documented csStores, csOriginal, csReorderMode, csModalMode, csModalStoreId, and csModalCreateDir but omitted the two lifecycle-management variables csClickHandler and csTriggerElement. The new entry describes the variable's purpose and its WCAG 2.1 SC 3.2.2 relationship, consistent with the verbosity level of neighboring entries. Non-behavioral — comment only.

[documentation-forward] csClickHandler is also absent from the module-level state comment block (L11-22) — this gap predates this WP. Add a brief description (e.g. 'csClickHandler: click-outside listener attached while modal is open; removed on csCloseModal()') alongside the other variable descriptions.

QA correctly identified that csRenderStoreModal() called while a modal is already open overwrites csTriggerElement with document.activeElement at re-render time (likely a modal input). This is a pre-existing architectural choice — no AC is violated. If focus management is hardened in future WPs, this re-render path should either: (a) preserve the original csTriggerElement if csTriggerElement is already non-null, or (b) call csCloseModal() before re-rendering. Not a blocker here.

notes: All three acceptance criteria are met. The implementation follows the established ES5 module-level state pattern exactly. The `typeof .focus === 'function'` guard covers both document.body and detached DOM elements as specified in the WP. No new dependencies, no new patterns introduced.
The only touch point is config-stores.js — three minimal, surgical edits. 3944 tests pass with zero regressions.
